purpose: Internal-RC low-frequency-clock variant of the dual-hatch image. Survives a dead or absent external 32.768 kHz crystal (LFXO).

parent.source_delta: prj_xiao_ble_sense_devkitv2-adafruit.conf ONLY. `diff -rq` over the two source trees reports exactly one differing file. No C source, no overlay, no CMakeLists, no board file changed.

the_hypothesis_this_image_tests.observed: Running firmware never starts the BLE radio. Disassembly puts the failure at bt_enable(); __init_hci_driver_init sits in the init slot immediately after __init_usb_init - USB alive, radio dead.
mechanism_confirmed_by_reading_the_pinne: zephyr/boards/arm/xiao_ble/xiao_ble_sense_defconfig does NOT pin K32SRC, and the application prj.conf did not either, so the parent build resolved to XTAL purely by that Kconfig default.
nrf/subsys/mpsl/init/mpsl_init.c forwards the choice into mpsl_init() and sets clock_cfg.skip_wait_lfclk_started = IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_SYSTEM_CLOCK_NO_WAIT).

CONFIG_SYSTEM_CLOCK_NO_WAIT is absent from the parent autoconf.h, so skip_wait_lfclk_started == false and mpsl_init() WAITS for LFCLKSTARTED. A crystal that never starts is therefore a hard stop inside mpsl_init(), upstream of bt_enable() succeeding.
Zephyr 3.4 ignores a failed mpsl_init in the SYS_INIT slot, so the failure is silent.

minimum_lf_clock_accuracy.verbatim: @retval -NRF_EPERM Unable to initialize because - MPSL is not initialized - MPSL needs to be configured with a LFCLK accuracy of 500 ppm or better.
minimum_lf_clock_accuracy.path_of_the_value: CONFIG_CLOCK_CONTROL_NRF_ACCURACY -> clock_cfg.accuracy_ppm (mpsl_init.c) -> mpsl_init() -> forwarded to the SoftDevice Controller
minimum_lf_clock_accuracy.why_500_and_not_250: 500 is the largest value sdc_init() accepts, and it is also what Kconfig.nrf itself defaults to for RC ('default CLOCK_CONTROL_NRF_K32SRC_500PPM if CLOCK_CONTROL_NRF_K32SRC_RC'). accuracy_ppm is a DECLARATION to the peer - the central sizes its receive window from it. Understating a calibrated LFRC's drift as MPSL_DEFAULT_CLOCK_ACCURACY_PPM (250) would shrink that window and risk dropped connections. 500 ppm is both honest for LFRC and legal for sdc_init().
minimum_lf_clock_accuracy.residual_note: 500 sits exactly on the documented boundary. If sdc_init() ever returns -NRF_EPERM on hardware, this declaration is the first thing to look at.

not_changed_and_why.CONFIG_SYSTEM_CLOCK_NO_WAIT: left unset. It only matters for a clock source that might not start; LFRC always starts. Setting it would add risk for no gain.
not_changed_and_why.CONFIG_CLOCK_CONTROL_NRF_DRIVER_CALIBRAT: resolves to n because CONFIG_CLOCK_CONTROL_NRF_FORCE_ALT=y (selected by CONFIG_CLOCK_CONTROL_MPSL in nrf/drivers/mpsl/clock_control/Kconfig). MPSL owns the clock and runs calibration itself via mpsl_calibration_work_handler; the Zephyr driver's own calibration path is correctly excluded.
not_changed_and_why.temperature_sensor: CONFIG_TEMP_NRF5_MPSL=1 was already present in the parent, so the temperature source calibration needs is already wired. No new dependency was pulled in.

residual_risks: NOT PROVEN ON HARDWARE. This receipt proves the image asks MPSL for the internal RC oscillator with legal calibration settings. It does not prove the radio comes up, because the LFXO hypothesis itself is still a hypothesis.

If the real fault is NOT the crystal (for example a corrupted MPSL/SDC region, a brown-out, or an antenna/RF front-end fault), this image will fail exactly like the parent and that failure is itself the diagnostic signal.
500 ppm is exactly the documented sdc_init() boundary. Legal, but with zero margin.

Higher sleep current than the crystal build: LFRC plus an HFXO-referenced calibration every 4-8 s. Battery life will be measurably worse. Acceptable for a recovery/diagnostic image, not necessarily for production.
Wider connection receive window (500 ppm vs 50 ppm declared) means slightly higher power on both ends and marginally worse worst-case latency.

Inherited from the parent: USB VID/PID are Zephyr test defaults (0x2FE3/0x100); the legacy DFU control point is unauthenticated by design in this bridge image (denial of service only); RAM at 68.19% of 256 KB.

Inherited from the parent: watchdog timeout is 900000 ms, a defensive value chosen because it is unverified whether the installed Adafruit bootloader feeds the watchdog it inherits across a soft reset.
